plain: To make a wrong seem less serious, as with extenuating circumstances

webster.text: To make thin, lean or slender.

more.text: To lessen; to diminish; as a crime or guilt.
To lessen in representation; to palliate; opposed to aggravate.
To lessen or diminish in honor.
To make thin or rare; opposed to condense.

example.quote: Let him now be confronted with the evidence of the fact, and let him, if he be able, justify or extenuate the shameful outrage he has offered to the dictates of truth and to the rules of fair dealing.
